problem: The existing one-minus-probability nonconformity rounds distinct tiny positive probabilities to 1.0 in floating point. A rounded calibration quantile can then include every world although many probabilities are strictly below the actual calibration cutoff.
change: Add an explicit probability-floor calibration method. Aggregate the minimum true-world probability per family, sort descending and use the same finite-sample rank ceil((n+1)*(1-alpha)). Include a world when p >= floor. Undersized calibration uses floor0 and still returns all worlds. Preserve existing default method and all existing calibration artifacts.
mathematical_scope: This is the monotone-equivalent finite-sample rule evaluated without subtractive cancellation. It does not alter the rank, alpha, model probabilities, labels, family grouping or exchangeability assumptions. It cannot recover probabilities already underflowed to zero.
verification: Test tiny-probability distinction, inclusive ties, minimum-over-family aggregation, insufficient calibration, invalid inputs, artifact binding, and equivalence to the old method away from cancellation. No model qualification or narrower real-world coverage guarantee follows.
